s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal mass with mild discomfort during exercise
salient_findings: Painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
Solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass on scrotal ultrasonography
key_facts: 16-year-old male with no prior medical history
Noted a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier
Denies any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
Lump’s size remained unchanged over two months
Experienced mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
Painless mass on physical examination
Testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
Mass contained two small hypoechoic foci
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers were all within normal limits

shortlist.label: Epididymal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of painless scrotal mass

shortlist.label: Spermatocele
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to epididymal cyst, possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor of the epididymis, matches clinical findings

shortlist.label: Epididymal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category including adenomatoid tumor, plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Papillary cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, benign tumor of the epididymis, cannot be ruled out

raw.rationale: The presence of a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic mass at the tail of the epididymis with hypoechoic foci, as seen on ultrasonography, is consistent with an adenomatoid tumor, which is a common benign tumor of the epididymis in young men.

rejected.label: Epididymal cyst
rejected.why: Epididymal cysts are typically fluid-filled and anechoic on ultrasonography, which does not match the solid, hyperechoic mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Spermatocele
rejected.why: Spermatoceles are cystic structures that contain sperm and are typically anechoic on ultrasonography, which does not match the solid mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Epididymal tumor
rejected.why: While the term 'epididymal tumor' could encompass adenomatoid tumors, it is too broad and does not specifically point to a benign tumor as likely as adenomatoid tumor given the clinical and ultrasonographic findings.

rejected.label: Papillary cystadenoma
rejected.why: Papillary cystadenoma is more commonly associated with the testis and has a different ultrasonographic appearance, often with septations and a more complex structure.
